About AsiaJCIS The Asia Joint Conference on Information Security (AsiaJCIS) is one of the premier annual international conferences on information security in the Asian region. It brings together researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and government to present and discuss new results on the technical and practical aspects of security. History AsiaJCIS began in 2006 as the Joint Workshop on Information Security (JWIS) and was renamed the Asia Joint Conference on Information Security (AsiaJCIS) in 2012. It has been held every year since 2006, rotating among its four host countries — Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and China . AsiaJCIS 2027, hosted by Juntendo University in Japan, will be the 22nd edition. A full list of past conferences and their locations is shown in the table above. Scope The conference covers a broad range of topics in information security, including cryptography, network security, system and application security, AI security, digital forensics, and privacy-enhancing technologies. See the current Call for Papers for the full list of topics. Program and Proceedings The conference adopts a double-blind peer review process, and since 2023 the technical program has included both regular papers and short papers . Proceedings of the IEEE-published editions (2012–2024) are available on IEEE Xplore and indexed by DBLP from 2012 onward; the most recent editions have been published via EasyChair . Per-year links are listed in the table above.

docs.text: Code of Conduct AsiaJCIS 2027 aims to provide a respectful, safe, and welcoming environment for everyone. All participants — including attendees, speakers, authors, organizers, and sponsors — are expected to behave professionally and courteously, and to refrain from harassment, discrimination, or disruptive conduct, both at the venue and online. Exclusion of Antisocial Forces The conference does not tolerate any involvement of antisocial forces (organized crime groups and related parties). The organizers reserve the right to refuse participation, registration, or sponsorship from any individual or organization that belongs to, or is associated with, antisocial forces, and to decline or return any such contribution. Right to Decline Participation The organizers reserve the right, at their sole discretion, to decline or cancel any registration, participation, or sponsorship , including where a person or organization has acted — or is likely to act — in a way that harms the conference, its participants, or its reputation, or where participation would conflict with this Code of Conduct. Disclaimer Participation in the conference is at each participant's own risk. The organizers are not responsible for any loss, damage, injury, or expense incurred during or in connection with the conference — including to personal belongings, or relating to travel, accommodation, or visa matters — and participants are encouraged to arrange their own insurance. The organizers are not a party to, and accept no responsibility for, disputes between participants, or between participants and sponsors. Reporting If you experience or witness a violation, please contact the organizers (see the Contact page). Reports will be handled discreetly, and the organizers may take appropriate action, including removal from the conference without a refund.

docs.text: Call for Papers Download the Call for Papers (PDF) The 22nd Asia Joint Conference on Information Security (AsiaJCIS 2027) Juntendo University, Japan · August 3–4, 2027 The 22nd Asia Joint Conference on Information Security (AsiaJCIS 2027) will be held at Juntendo University, Japan. This conference focuses on the technical and practical aspects of security applications and will serve as a forum to present new results from the academic research community and the industry. Original papers are solicited for submission to AsiaJCIS. In addition, several distinguished security experts will be invited to give technical talks. Topics Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: Cryptography: Post Quantum Cryptography, Quantum Cryptography, Applied Cryptography, Cryptanalysis and Side Channel Attack, Blockchain and Smart Contract Security Network Security: Cloud Computing Security, NGN Security, Home Computing and Smart Home Security, Mobile Security, Ad-Hoc and Wireless Sensor Network Security, VANET Security, Wireless PAN/LAN/MAN/WAN Security, Peer-to-peer Computing Security, FW/IDS/IPS, DoS/DDoS Attack Countermeasures, Leak Detection, 5G/6G Mobile Communication, Zero Trust System Security: Computer/Application Security, Virtual Machine Security, Database Security, Secure eHealth/eCommerce, Smart Contract, Ubiquitous Computing Security, Internet of Things (IoT) Application Security: Email Security, Web Services Security, SNS Security, Mobile Security, IPTV Security, Software Supply Chain Security, AI Security and Privacy Information Security Management: Human Resource Security, Big Data, Trusted Computing, Data Breach, Intrusion Detection, Phishing, Privacy Breach, Privacy-Enhancing Technology Others: Smart Grid Security, Malware Countermeasures, Content Management, Biometrics, Usable Security and Privacy, Outsourcing Management, Fake News Instructions for Authors Authors are invited to submit original papers. The papers must not substantially duplicate work that any authors have published elsewhere or have submitted in parallel to any other conferences with proceedings. This conference adopts a double-blind peer review. The submitted manuscripts must be anonymous, with no author names, affiliations, acknowledgements, or obvious references. Authors of accepted papers MUST give an oral presentation at the conference. Papers of authors who will not attend the conference will be deleted from the conference proceedings and announced as no-show papers on the conference site. This year, we will have regular papers and short papers. Once accepted, the program committee will decide whether the paper will be presented as a regular or short paper. The paper submission should conform to the following guidelines: The submission must be written in English and submitted in PDF format. The page limit, template, and formatting details will be announced together with the submission website. Authors should follow the official conference template once it is available. Submissions ignoring these guidelines may be rejected without further consideration. Important Dates Event Date Paper Submission Deadline Friday, April 16, 2027 (AoE) Notification of Acceptance May 28, 2027 Camera-Ready Deadline Friday, June 18, 2027 (AoE) Conference Dates August 3–4, 2027 Note All deadlines are 23:59 AoE (Anywhere on Earth). Submission-related deadlines are tentative and may be adjusted; the conference dates (August 3–4, 2027) are confirmed. Submission Site The submission site (EasyChair) will be announced shortly. Papers must be submitted in PDF format through EasyChair. Publication Accepted papers are planned to be published through IEEE Conference Publishing Services (CPS) and submitted for inclusion in IEEE Xplore. Committees See the Committee page for the full list of chairs and committee members.

docs.text: Call for Sponsors AsiaJCIS 2027 AsiaJCIS 2027 welcomes sponsorship from industry and academic organizations. Sponsoring the conference is an excellent opportunity to support the information security research community across Asia and to raise your organization's visibility among researchers and practitioners from Japan, Korea, Taiwan, China, and beyond. Why Sponsor Connect with security researchers and practitioners from academia, industry, and government. Display your banner at the venue and place brochures or flyers for participants. Show your logo on the conference website and on-site. Support students and the next generation of security researchers. Sponsorship Levels The planned tiers are shown below. Payment is accepted in Japanese yen (JPY) or US dollars (USD) . Level JPY USD (approx.) Benefits Platinum ¥200,000 $1,400 Large banner (prime placement) at the venue; brochure/flyer placed at the venue; logo on the website and on-site; acknowledgment in the opening/closing sessions Gold ¥100,000 $700 Medium banner at the venue; brochure/flyer placed at the venue; logo on the website and on-site Silver ¥50,000 $350 Small banner at the venue; logo on the website and on-site Banner size and prominence scale with the sponsorship level. Sponsors may also place brochures or flyers in the venue for participants. Banner specifications (dimensions and format) will be provided to sponsors in advance. Additional Options (by arrangement) The following are available on request, subject to availability and the venue layout. If any of these are of interest, please contact us early to discuss. Exhibition booth or demonstration at the venue. Coffee/tea break naming — for example, "Refreshments sponsored by …" displayed at the refreshment area (a limited number of breaks). Amounts are tentative and may be adjusted. USD figures are approximate equivalents shown for convenience; the exact USD amount will be confirmed closer to the conference. Individual Supporters Support is not limited to organizations — individuals are also warmly welcome . Individual contributions start from just ¥1,000 (or the equivalent in USD). With your consent, your name will be listed as a supporter on the conference website. This is a simple way for members of the community to help sustain AsiaJCIS. How to Become a Sponsor or Supporter Organizations and individuals interested in supporting AsiaJCIS 2027 are invited to get in touch. Please see the Contact page; a dedicated sponsorship contact and payment details (bank transfer, etc.) will be announced shortly. All sponsorships are subject to acceptance by the organizers. Please also see our Code of Conduct . Sponsors & Supporters Sponsors and individual supporters will be listed here (with their consent) as they are confirmed.

docs.text: Travel & Visa AsiaJCIS 2027 Getting There The conference is held at Juntendo University, Urayasu-Hinode Campus, on the Tokyo Bay waterfront. From Haneda Airport (HND): about 40 minutes (recommended for international arrivals). From Narita Airport (NRT): about 60 minutes. From Tokyo Station: about 20 minutes by train to Shin-Urayasu Station, then about 10 minutes by bus. A shuttle bus for participants is being planned. See the Venue page for the map and detailed access. Visa Information Participants who require a visa to enter Japan are responsible for arranging their own visa. Please check the requirements with the Japanese embassy or consulate in your country or region well in advance , as processing can take several weeks. Whether a visa is granted is decided solely by the Japanese immigration authorities and the relevant embassy or consulate . The organizers have no influence over visa decisions and cannot guarantee that a visa will be issued . Letter of Invitation Upon request, the organizers can provide a letter of invitation (or a letter of participation) to support a visa application. Please note: Letters are issued only to authors of accepted papers who have completed registration and to registered participants . A letter only confirms the person's association with the conference. It does not imply any financial responsibility on the part of the organizers, and does not guarantee that a visa will be approved. Requests should be made after registration. Please allow sufficient time before your intended travel date. To request a letter, please see the Contact page.

docs.text: Venue AsiaJCIS 2027 Conference Venue Juntendo University, Urayasu-Hinode Campus , Chiba, Japan. 6-8-1 Hinode, Urayasu, Chiba 279-0013, Japan （〒279-0013 千葉県浦安市日の出6-8-1） The campus opened in 2022 and is located on the Tokyo Bay waterfront, within easy reach of central Tokyo and both international airports. Open in Google Maps Access From Haneda Airport (HND): about 40 minutes. From Narita Airport (NRT): about 60 minutes. From Tokyo Station: about 20 minutes by train to Shin-Urayasu Station, then about 10 minutes by bus. Tokyo Disney Resort is located at the neighboring station, and can be a convenient transfer point. A shuttle bus for conference participants is being planned. Haneda Airport is recommended for international arrivals. Detailed directions and the shuttle schedule will be announced closer to the conference. Explore the Area The campus sits right on the Tokyo Bay waterfront , and central Tokyo is only about 20 minutes away — so it is easy to combine the conference with some sightseeing. Tokyo Disney Resort is at the neighboring station (Maihama). Arriving a day early or staying on afterwards is a popular option. Central Tokyo is within easy reach: Tokyo Station (~20 min), and from there Asakusa (Sensō-ji temple), Ginza, Akihabara, and more. Tokyo Bay offers waterfront walks and views, with large bayside parks nearby. Plan your visit: Things to do in Urayasu (TripAdvisor) · Urayasu tourism (official) · Shin-Urayasu area guide (Japanese) Food The bay area is known for fresh seafood and sushi , and Japan's casual izakaya pubs are a great way to unwind after sessions. A conference banquet featuring local seafood is planned — see the Social Program below. Good to Know Season: the conference is in early August. Tokyo summers are warm and humid, so light clothing is recommended. It is also the season of summer festivals ( matsuri ) and fireworks. Getting around: trains are frequent and signposted in English; a rechargeable IC card (Suica / PASMO / Welcome Suica) makes travel easy. Hotels: there are many hotels around Maihama and Shin-Urayasu, from business hotels to bayside resorts (see the Accommodation page). Social Program A conference banquet featuring local seafood is planned, together with time for networking among participants. Details will be announced closer to the conference.
